content:
The test image shows a longitudinally split tomato stem with:
- Hollowed/collapsed internal pith tissue (tan/white, fibrous)
- Dark black bodies visible inside the stem cavity (sclerotia)
- Surrounding dead/dried stem tissue

This strongly suggests a stem disease with sclerotia. Top candidates: **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**, **Southern_Blight**, **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**.

Now viewing one reference from each candidate:

This is very informative. The Sclerotinia reference (Bugwood_16.jpg, #5593852) shows isolated sclerotia — hard, black, irregularly-shaped bodies. The test image (#5593851, consecutive Bugwood number) shows a split stem with identical dark sclerotia inside the hollow pith cavity. These are from the same source series.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: longitudinally split stem, hollow/fibrous tan pith, dark black sclerotia bodies inside — classic Sclerotinia stem rot presentation
- Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot reference: exact sclerotia match (Bugwood 5593852 vs test 5593851 — consecutive)
- Southern_Blight: white mycelium at soil level, different pattern
- Alternaria: external dark stem canker, no internal sclerotia
